item.title: Introduction
item.description:
Atomic Habits#

This serves as a reference to all the material covered as a part of the atomic habits seminar.

James Clear Articles#

Here is a link to some James Clear articles

Habits#

It is important for you to form the habits that will lead you to be the person you want to be. The discovery of this identity is first and foremost in your journey to adopt better and newer habits.

item.title: Quizzes
item.description:
Quizzes#

The quizzes for each section of the seminar.

Quiz 1#

  1. Name the three layers of behavior change, from outermost to innermost. In which direction does lasting change occur?
  2. What should your primary focus be?
    • A) What you want to achieve
    • B) Who you wish to become
    • C) How quickly you can get there
    • D) What others expect of you
  3. “Identity First” implies ______________________________.
  4. “Cast Votes” implies ______________________________.
  5. “Language Shift” expects ______________________________.

Quiz 2#

  1. List the four stages of the Habit Loop, in order.
  2. Dopamine spikes at the _____ .
  3. Which type of reward spikes dopamine the hardest?
  4. “Just one more scroll” is hard to resist because the loop is built around a _____ .

Quiz 3#

  1. What do winners and losers have in common?
  2. A _____ is the direction and a _____ is the vehicle.
  3. Give four reasons why goal-only thinking is a problem.
  4. What problem do you see in each of the below examples for goal setting (as mentioned in the section)?
    • a. “Bill Gates dropped out of school to start Microsoft”
    • b. “I won the district level 100m sprint”
    • c. “I will be at peace once I get a Duke bike”
    • d. “I want to lose 8kgs of weight and today is the 4th day”

Quiz 4#

  1. Name the four laws of behavioural change.
  2. Which law does each of the following associate with?
    • a. Shrink the habit until starting takes no willpower
    • b. Design the cue so it’s impossible to miss
    • c. Make the win felt right away, every time
    • d. Pair the habit with something you already crave
  3. What are the three problems of relying on motivation?

Quiz 5#

  1. Give an example of how to apply Law 1 to build each of these habits:
    • A. Running
    • B. Keeping the fridge stocked with healthy food
    • C. Learning to play the guitar
    • D. Reading books
  2. Design the room ____________ .

Quiz 6#

  1. List the three groups of social influence.
  2. Name the influence group for each of the following:
    • a. We imitate people with status, hoping their behavior earns us the same respect
    • b. Family, partners, close friends shape what feels “normal” more than anyone else
    • c. A group pulls you toward its average without you noticing
  3. Give an example for temptation bundling.
  4. Give an example for habit stacking.
  5. Pair the hard thing with something _________ .

Quiz 7#

  1. Name the three tactics under “Make It Easy” covered in this section.
  2. The two-minute rule says: ________ .
  3. What’s the difference between “priming the environment” and “shrinking the habit”? Give one word or short phrase for each.
  4. The hardest part of any habit is ______ .
  5. Shrink it until _________ .
  6. Give the comparison between taking two minutes vs waiting for the mood once the cue appears.
  7. Phone lock-out after 10 pm is _____ tactic.
  8. Automate: a one time decision replaces _____ .

Quiz 8#

  1. Law 4 is about _____ .
  2. Name the three tactics this section teaches _____ .
  3. What gets rewarded ______ .
  4. How does marking an “X” on a calendar help?
  5. What’s an example of rewarding it immediately? Why does it work over reward it later?
  6. What is a tactic that results in your friend messaging whether you went for a run? Why is it important?
  7. Never let a good rep ____ .

Quiz 9#

  1. The section’s core rule: “Miss once _________ "
  2. What actually has the potential to kill a habit?
  3. If you skip a habit today, what happens tomorrow?
  4. The ice cube example is used to explain what about habits?
  5. What should you do during the flat stretch?
  6. What’s the difference between perfection and identity as the goal of a habit?
  7. One percent better daily = ___________ times.
  8. One percent worse daily = ___________ times.

Quiz 10#

  1. To break a bad habit ______ the four laws.
  2. Make the four laws relevant for this section and list them.
  3. Apply the laws to get off Instagram (give tactics).
  4. How to use “mark the calendar” to get off a bad habit?
  5. Why is a written witnessed contract better than a private promise to yourself?
  6. Give examples for the tactics of the four laws for this section.

item.title: Habit Challenge Cards
item.description:
Habit Challenge Cards#

Each card is a scenario. Your team designs the system that solves it, using the four laws — make it obvious, attractive, easy, and satisfying. For the cards under Breaking a Bad Habit, invert them: make it invisible, unattractive, hard, and unsatisfying.

Building a Good Habit#

Daily Reading Habit#

Your team is handed a fresh grad who reads zero pages a week. Design a system that gets them into a sustainable daily reading habit.
